question: Samia set off on her bicycle to visit her friend, traveling at an average speed of \(17\) kilometers per hour. When she had gone half the distance to her friend’s house, a tire went flat, and she walked the rest of the way at \(5\) kilometers per hour. In all it took her \(44\) minutes to reach her friend’s house. In kilometers rounded to the nearest tenth, how far did Samia walk?
solution:
Samia bicycled and walked equal distances, so let each distance be \(d\) kilometers. Using time equals distance divided by speed, she bicycled for \(d/17\) hours and walked for \(d/5\) hours.

Her total time was \(44/60=11/15\) hours, so
\[
\frac{d}{17}+\frac{d}{5}=\frac{11}{15}.
\]
Multiplying by the common denominator \(255\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
15d+51d&=187,\\
66d&=187,\\
d&=\frac{187}{66}=\frac{17}{6}=2.8333\ldots.
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore Samia walked \(\boxed{2.8}\) kilometers to the nearest tenth, choice \(\text{C}\).
